vigraha-tattva: And today we want to discuss the glories of vigraha-tattva, the glories of the deity. Caitanya Mahāprabhu has taught the glories of the deity by His own life and example.
vigraha-not-idol: So, what is arcā-vigraha, the deity? The deity is not called an idol because idolatry means to imagine some speculation of what God is like and then to carve an image and worship that and think that it's God or think that it represents, it's a symbol of something higher. So all of these people have these different ideas, but none of these ideas are correct in regard to the vigraha. So we want to discuss this. The word vigraha means vi means viśeṣa and graha means grahaṇa, to accept. So vigraha, the form of the Supreme Lord who appears in this world, especially to accept our loving services is called vigraha. So in Caitanya-caritāmṛta it is said,
vigraha-sac-cid-ananda: And so, what is vigraha? The deity is not stone. The deity is not wood or metal. But rather, the sat-cit-ānanda-vigraha, the eternal, conscious, blissful form of the Supreme Lord.
vigraha-fourth-form: So, we can know that Paramātmā is there, but still in our condition state, we cannot hear Him. We cannot see Him. We cannot interact with Him. So, God in the spiritual world is merciful. His avatāras are merciful, and Paramātmā in the heart, these three svarūpas, they are all there, and they're merciful, but they're not accessible to us. Therefore, the Lord appears in the fourth form, that is, arcā-vigraha. The deity. How kind. The deity appears in this world in such a way that we can interact with Him using the resources which are even available to us in our conditioned state. So we should know that in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, there it is said,
vigraha-service-for-all: We can easily approach Him and serve Him. Even if a person is poor, they may think, but I cannot offer so many opulent things. I don't have hundreds of flowers to offer (..) many garlands every day. I don't have so many gold and jeweled ornaments. But vigraha is so kind. Even if you'll serve the vigraha in your mind. You may only have some simple rice and dal. But when you offer it, it's free. You can think, I am offering Krishna the rasagullas and gulābjāmuns and pakorās and so many. (..) If you can afford to make them all yourself, you should do this. If you don't, then it becomes aparādha, the fault of miserliness. If a person has the facility but they don't use their wealth in the service of the deity, becomes aparādha, the fault of miserliness. But if a person is a virakta, very poor, simple sādhu, renounced person, then they may offer simple things. Krishna said,
vigraha-three-senses: So, it is only when the sarvottama-vastu, when the highest reality is the mādhurya, the sweetness of the highest reality is relished through all three types of senses, antaḥkaraṇa, jñānendriya and karmendriya, that the āsvādana, that means tasting is pūrṇa. you see? So, there is a pūrṇa-āsvādanam.
vigraha-diksa: So all those who have received dīkṣā from a sad-guru, and they those who are sat-śiṣya, real disciples who have received dīkṣā from sad-guru, real guru, they have transcendental bodies in which they serve the Supreme Lord and they have the pūrṇa-āsvādana, (..) pūrṇa-mādhurya-āsvādana, the full taste of the sweetness of the supreme truth by serving the vigraha and by chanting Harināma. So, something to note here, which is so important. Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, he said,
vigraha-not-symbol: Then the second type of path which is done by the jñānīs who have an impersonal knowledge, (..) they want impersonal knowledge, that is called pratīkopāsanā. So pratīka is the idea that if you're worshiping something with a form, then (..) you should do this because that is just like a technique to control your mind. Because it's very difficult to concentrate on the emptiness, on empty light. So let me have a statue or a maṇḍala or something, some crystals or something like that. Or I can worship the sun, or the earth, or the fire, or water, or (..) air, space, is everywhere. It's big. So people accept something to be a pratīka, that's a representative of God, and they try to focus their mind on that. So, this will also not give any ānanda, any joy, because all of these things that they're meditating, they are inert and limited material objects. So there'll be no the mādhurya-āsvādana at all, what to speak of a pūrṇa-mādhurya-anubhava. It's impossible. So, we don't worship pratīka, a symbol. And it should be understood in Vedānta-sūtra it is said,
vigraha-four-madhuris: But even that Krishna in who (..) on driving the chariot of Krishna, He does not have the four mādhurīs of Krishna in Vṛndāvana. So our ācāryas are so kind, so merciful, and they have manifested that Krishna of Vṛndāvana who has the rūpa-mādhurī, (..) of His form, veṇu-mādhurī, the sweetness of His flute, the prema-mādhurī, the sweetness of His loving associates because Krishna is not alone. His most loving associate is there, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī. Who has more prema than Rādhikā, no one. And līlā-mādhurī, that Krishna has the all the sweetest pastimes. And so we see that in the service of the deity, there is the pūrṇa-mādhurya-āsvādana and not in any other path or any other (..) object of service.
vigraha-darsana-greed: This is darśana of the vigraha. But we would not know it unless we hear. Now that's the topic we were discussing. That serving, seeing the deity, the sweetness of the deity, along with hearing, these two together, they're so effective for awakening greed. Hearing can be effective by itself. But only darśana of the deity will not be effective by itself. But if it's performed along with hearing and every time you come before Rādhā and Krishna and the saṁskāras of this sweet kathā are raised in the heart, then the greed will intensify every day. So how merciful is the vigraha.
vigraha-tota-gopinatha:
So one day, Krishna, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he came to Yameśvara-ṭoṭā and he was sitting on the earth in the sand. It's very sandy there in the sand dunes by the ocean.

Mahāprabhu was sitting in the sand and he was drawing in the sand with his fingernail. And as he was drawing in the sand, tears were flowing from his eyes like the Ganges, like Gaṅgā. And his eyes were so filled with tears, he could not see anything. Aśru-gaṅgā netre vahe, kichu nāhi dekhi. And he could not see anything. He was only feeling around in the sand and drawing with his fingernail. And as he was touching the sand, he touched something. And then he began to move some sand with his hands. And then he was so surprised. And he got up and went to Gadādhara Paṇḍita who was nearby and said, "Hey Gadādhara, I want to give you something from my heart. Will you accept it?" Gadādhara Paṇḍita said, "Surely I must accept it." Mahāprabhu said, "Oh, Gadādhara, come with me." And he took the hand of Gadādhara and brought him to that place. And he began to remove the sand, and there was Gopīnātha. The vigraha of Gopīnātha in Yameśvara-ṭoṭā, so his name is Ṭoṭā-gopīnātha.
applying-tilaka: This is the desire. This is the desire of all the Rūpānuga Vaiṣṇavas, only that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will meet together. This is why we put tilaka on every day, you see? One side is Rādhikā, one side means Kṛṣṇa. They're parallel lines, so the parallel lines don't meet. But these parallel lines are meeting where, here, this is a tulasī leaf, represents Vṛndā.
waking-the-lord: At that time in the early morning, the mañjarīs, they were awake almost the whole night, but just towards the end of the night, they lie down on the—in the courtyard, just outside the kuñja. And then suddenly, (..) Maidservant wakes up and looks around because she's afraid, "Oh, did I oversleep? Did I miss my service?" And then she looks around, sees, "Oh, others are still resting, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are still sleeping." Sigh. Relief. "I thought—for a moment I was very anxious, but now I see there's still time." So then that devotee is remembering his spiritual form, will get up and go and wake up Gurudeva. Understand? That means wake up another sakhī, another other mañjarīs who are there. And then go to see, uṭho, nidrā chāḍi’ uṭha jīva, "Oh, my life and soul, wake up." And they'll go, and they look inside: "Oh, in this beautiful kuñja-bhavana, this pavilion of flowers in the forest of Vṛndāvana on the bank of Yamunā, see Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Śyāmasundara resting there."
morning-bhoga-arati: But the problem is that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa cannot go home being decorated in the sambhoga-cihna. So they'll have to be, (..) (..) removed. And that's why the pujārī in maṅgala-ārati is coming with a water and a cloth. So first she puts the water in the conch, that means the maidservants are coming and putting some, (..) fresh, fragrant water on the bodies of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and taking the cloth and wiping away the sambhoga-cihna. But as they wipe away As this As these cihna are the signs of sambhoga meeting, then as they're being wiped away, that means it's as if they are erasing the pastime itself. And it's awakening the vipralambha-bhāva. When the sambhoga-cihna is wiped away, when meeting is wiped away, then you are left with separation. This is the bhāva of maṅgala-ārati. So the devotees are watching the ārati and seeing the offering of the water, the offering of the cloth like this, and the nectar of the union is being wiped away, and the pain of separation is rising up in the heart.
srngara-arati: So each and every aspect of Rādhārāṇī's body, and cosmetics, and ornaments—ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgāra, sixteen types of cosmetics, and dvādaśa-ābharaṇa, twelve types of golden ornaments—they're all various bhāvas of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She's decorated in jewels; Her jewels are prema-vaicittya, (..) Her sparkling jewels are the separation She feels in Kṛṣṇa's presence. So all of these things make Her svarūpa beautiful. So when you're decorating your Deities, just remember that all the śṛṅgāra was not bought from Loi Bazaar. Forget that! This śṛṅgāra is actually the all the various aspects of Rādhikā's mahā-bhāva. And then your service becomes rasamayī sevā.
raja-bhoga-offering: So, after receiving dīkṣā from guru, one is allowed to serve the vigraha. Because (^)the deity form of vigraha that (..) in which we see the vigraha, this is the manifestation in this world of the mantropāsanāmayī-līlā-pīṭha. We want to (..) enter into that līlā-pīṭha, but it's hard for us to meditate upon this, because you cannot see it. So, Guru said, “Oh, look, the Vigraha are here.” Now you can see. And even you can do this (..) yoga-pīṭha-sevā. Here is all the paraphernalia that the sakhī is used. So, under guidance of guru-rūpa-sakhī, you should meditate by the way you serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in this līlā-pīṭha, and bring your paraphernalia and do ārati. It includes the devotees doing ārati and those who are also watching; all take part and enter into this līlā-pīṭha. This is why in a temple, morning, noon, and evening ārati, three times a day, all the devotees are going to make this saṁskāra, (^)that gives the impression so that they can meditate on this.
putting-deities-to-rest-noon: If you serve your deities you can realize this. Vigraha. Because, though Kṛṣṇa, He can do everything Himself, but in the form of vigraha He stands very still. "You have to do everything for Me. You can make Me lie down, make Me stand up, bring Me food." Out of love He's not moving. But in your mind you thinking, "He's not moving because He's made out of metal." Don't think! You're thinking, "Kṛṣṇa's not talking." Why? Because He's remembering Rādhārāṇī, His voice is choked, He cannot say. If you serve your Ṭhākurajī you can realize it.
sandhya-arati:
So, the cāmara, this cāmara-sevā, so beautiful! Why is this cāmara-sevā so beautiful? Sometimes they don't even do the cāmara-sevā with a cāmara, they just open their hair and do it with their braids. And this cāmara-sevā is so beautiful because the cāmara has thousands and thousands of hairs. So, this cāmara or the braid represents (^)there are 72,000 nāḍīs in the body, you know, according to Vedānta-sūtra, there are 72,000 nāḍīs, they're the channels through which all your prāṇa moves. So, the mañjarīs are thinking, "This cāmara, all these hairs, these are my 72,000 nāḍīs, and I am serving Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa with all my prāṇas."

[…]

These are the signs of the emperor. There may be (..) many kings, but only the emperor and the empress, (^)the king and queen of the world are allowed to have the white cāmara and the white parasol. So, when the mañjarīs, they take the white cāmara and they fan Rādhikā... Ah!

[…]

Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura said if someone has abhimāna, that is a pride, so proud, "I am so proud to be the dāsī of Rādhikā," then they very easily attain Kṛṣṇa. Nothing to do, there's nothing to do to attain Kṛṣṇa. He'll be included in that like a free gift, (..) if someone just has the pride in the greatness of Rādhikā. So, this cāmara-sevā is just the hearts of the mañjarīs are exploding. Rādhikā is the empress of Vṛndāvana. There was the coronation, so (..) the rāja-abhiṣeka of Rādhikā when She became Vṛndāvaneśvarī. So proud of this. So, this is done with a great abhimāna.
putting-deities-to-rest-evening: And then in this verse, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, he's realizing in his heart, when he puts his deities to take rest at night, "Oh, my Gurudeva as Tulasī Mañjarī made this very beautiful bed. And now Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are reclining there after taking fresh fruits, and I'm massaging the feet of Rādhikā." So what began as following vaidhī-bhakti internally (..) became rāgānugā-bhakti and spontaneous realization.
worship-sixteen-articles: Then they made a deity of Kātyāyanī from clay on the bank of the river, here. And they offered 16 articles. And with every article, they were thinking of Kṛṣṇa. When they offered the incense, "O Kātyāyanī-devī, we're offering you this fragrant incense, please offer to our nostrils the fragrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa." "O Devī, we're offering this dīpas, these lights to you, please give us the shining light of the eyes of Kṛṣṇa." Like this, with every article that they're offering, they were begging Kātyāyanī to fulfill their desire to meet Kṛṣṇa.
atma-dhyana: I am sitting at the lotus feet of my guru. I'm wearing a divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandira-tilakam, beautiful tilaka. Harināma-subhagaṁ, my body is made with sandalwood paste (..) and the holy names, Radheshyam or Gaura Gadadhara or Hare Krishna painted on my body in sandalwood paste. I'm wearing very clean cloth and I'm sitting at the feet of guru and I am overwhelmed with intense enthusiasm to serve. This is called the ātma-jñāna mantra.
arcana-procedure: Actually, when a pūjārī, the priest who is serving the deity, offers any articles to the deity, actually, he should offer the articles first by in the mind. And so, he's thinking, "Oh, in my svarūpa with my guru-rūpa-sakhī, my Gurudeva in Her svarūpa, and I am passing the articles and together we are serving Rādhikā." So when you do ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā, worship with 16 articles, each one is done by mind first, and then the actual physical article is done.
10-abharana: Simple service. If you are a pūjārī and you serve the Deities, then every day then you have to take the jewelry and put the jewelry on the Deities, even in vaidhī-bhakti. But those who are in rāga-mārga, they also decorate the Deities every day, but remembering these beautiful verses, like Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī: kiṁ te syamantaka-maṇiṁ taralīkaromi(32). "When will I place this beautiful jewel as the main pendant on your necklace around your neck, like this?" But this is a bhāva-sevā, bhāva-sevā. That means it's not only dressing, but dressing Rādhikā in such a way that She becomes inspired, She's (..) inflamed with more and more desires to serve Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
offering-maha-prasada: Ucchiṣṭa means remnant. If Gurudeva is eating, then what is left on his plate, this is ucchiṣṭa, and the disciple wants to take the ucchiṣṭa, the remnant of Gurudeva. But the actual desire of taking the ucchiṣṭa is: "Oh, Gurudeva, when will you give me your ucchiṣṭa-sevā, the remnant of your service to Rādhikā?" So, this prayer, śrī-rūpa-mañjarī-karārcita-pāda-padma, is (..) very sweet, because Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī is praying for the ucchiṣṭa-sevā of his śikṣā-guru, Rūpa Gosvāmī. It is extraordinarily beautiful and sweet because it is the extremity of ānugatyamayī-sevā, being in ānugatya. Not only to serve under the guidance, but actually to take up the remnant of the very service. So, this is the picture of rūpānuga-bhajana.
arcana-sri-guru: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself had said, "Oh, don't serve Me first, serve your Gurudeva first. Worship your Gurudeva first, and then after that, you can worship Me. If you do this, then there's no doubt you'll attain siddhi, you'll become perfected. But if one does not worship his Gurudeva first, then everything is niṣphala, has no fruit at all." Why? Because we cannot trespass, we cannot force our way into the divine realm. Everything is by permission, by permission only. So first, we seek permission from Gurudeva to serve Gaurāṅga, and then we seek permission from Gaurāṅga to serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Only when They open the door to divine, (..) divine plane and accept us as Their near and dear one, as Their associate, then we can enter, otherwise not, by our own power it is completely impossible.
guru-arcana-procedure: Only offering a pile of flowers will not do. The flower is a symbol. The flower is very soft and fragrant. So, our heart should be very soft and fragrant like a flower. Fragrance means emanating so many loving moods. So, flower has no power to offer itself. But if the flower is in the hand of Śrī Guru, he can offer to the Deities. So, with an affectionate heart, we understand that we cannot move closer to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. But rather, if we offer our affectionate heart into the hand of Śrī Guru, then he can offer us to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. So, this is the meaning of offering a puṣpāñjali on Vyāsa-pūjā day.
offering-bhoga:
...and I am assisting him. So, just like Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī in the Rādhākānta Maṭha, in the Gambhīrā, actually has a Deity of his Gurudeva. And he would bring the Deity... and sit the Deity where actually... think he's the Deity is doing offering. So even today Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī sits on his āsana, and when it's time for the bhoga offering, the pūjārī picks up the Deity, carries him, and he does the pūjārī does everything, but the idea is that Gopāla Guru Gosvāmī is doing it. So that mood is there.

[…]

So this is the, um, ceremony for offering mahā-prasāda correctly for those who have the second initiation, because it's the beginning of the mānasī-sevā. That you're actually serving Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It's not that, uh, you get the food and you're giving and sending by a delivery very far away. But no, you are there in the kuñja with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and you are serving them with guru in the sakhī form, and other sakhīs as well. So it's beginning the internal services, manifested through the expression of arcana.
bhoga-procedure:
So, um, even here it's described how to offer flowers to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, invite them to come on the seat, and wash their hands and feet. So, but, uh, I'd like to add something which is not here. It's, but it's a very simple thing, and a basic thing. And that is that you do this ceremony first to guru.

[…]

Then you take, and then you offer them: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Offer the puṣpāñjali at the feet of Gurudeva. Then you take an āsana. So usually they have like this, some small seats. Um, if you only have pure Deities, it's okay, you can do by mind to guru, but if you have for guru, you can also use. So then, uh, ringing the bell and place the āsana in front of Gurudeva: idam āsanaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Then, uh, inviting Gurudeva: āvāhayāmi, that means come, and then sit down, sthāpayāmi, and then welcome: prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. Āvāhayāmi sthāpayāmi prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. And you meditate that from the picture of Gurudeva or the Deity of, he is coming now and sitting on the āsana. Understand? Now Gurudeva is there.
maha-prasad-distribution: So for pure devotees tasting mahā-prasāda is very ecstatic. Because, when Rādhikā is cooking, then all Her ecstatic love goes into those preparations. And when Kṛṣṇa tastes that, then what Rādhikā was feeling appears in His heart. And then He has new love for Rādhikā. Then (..) when Kṛṣṇa's remnants are taken back to Rādhikā... And Rādhikā tastes the remnant of Kṛṣṇa... Then She has a sphūrti, She has a realization... Of what Kṛṣṇa was realizing... When He was realizing what Rādhikā was realizing when She was cooking. So in this way, through mahā-prasādam, there is very beautiful meeting of the hearts of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. And then, when the mañjarīs, they take the remnant of Rādhikā... Then they realize what Rādhikā was realizing, when She was realizing what Kṛṣṇa was realizing, when He was realizing what She was realizing when She was... So in this mood we take prasādam. Then you are really, actually honoring prasādam and not just eating like feeding time at the farm.
mantras-honouring-caranamrita: We say this mantra as we take caraṇāmṛta. Oh, it destroys all kleśa, it destroys all of our sins, śuddha-bhakti-dam, and causes the appearance of pure devotion, the sphūrti of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and the sphūrti of all the pastimes, of the various cosmetics that were transferred from the body of Kṛṣṇa to the body of Rādhikā, and from the body of Rādhikā to the body of Kṛṣṇa, all these cosmetics of the beautiful pastimes have been washed into this caraṇāmṛta, and it can manifest those beautiful pastimes.
maha-abhiseka: How blissful it was (..) to do the abhiṣeka of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. By doing the abhiṣeka, that means showering Kṛṣṇa, then everyone felt that they were abhiṣikta, that means they themselves, they were taking shower in amṛta. Anyone can experience this. If you do abhiṣeka of Kṛṣṇa's deity or you do abhiṣeka of your own deities, then though you are showering Kṛṣṇa, you feel yourself as if your heart is being showered with nectar.
prayers-forgiveness: Aparādha-sahasra-bhājanam, "Oh Hari, I am very offensive, I am guilty of thousands and thousands of offenses, and I am fit to be punished. I am drowning in this fierce ocean of material existence. I am completely lost. Please make me Your own, ātmasāt kuru." Ātmasāt kuru. That means ātmasāt means that. (..) "I am Yours. I am not independent from You. I am completely dependent on You. May my heart be one with Your heart, ātmasāt. You have promised to deliver anyone who takes shelter of You. Therefore, please deliver me."
arati-ceremony: In rāga-mārga, one has to follow the associates. What is the mood of the sakhīs when they are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa? You see, even Mother Yaśodā, when Kṛṣṇa returns in the evening from taking the cows to graze, Mother Yaśodā and all the elderly mothers, they also offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa. So it cannot be because they think He's God. So (..) there's another meaning to ārati. Ārati is a reception when you receive someone, you welcome them in this way. But the bhāva of the, when a person is offering ārati, is that, "Oh my beloved, more dear to me than my prāṇa, whatever obstacles may come—you have overcome so many obstacles to be here together—but in the future if any obstacles will come due to fate, then let all those problems, let all those obstacles, may all those difficulties fall on my head, but let you be free from all inconveniences. You should not suffer." So when the sakhīs are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, it is, they're offering their own lives. This is a gesture that, "You should be happy, you should not have any problem, you, no ill-fate should come to you. Whatever ill-fate was meant to come to you, it should come to me instead, but let you be happy." This is the meaning of (..) the mood of ārati in Vraja, whether Mother Yaśodā is offering or whether Lalitā and the sakhīs are offering to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It's such an expression of love.
caturmasya-period: So many persons they begin their Cāturmāsya vrata today, but following Prabhupāda Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, we begin our Cāturmāsya from after four days time on the appearance day of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, Guru Pūrṇimā. Why? Because the final month is Kārtika, that is Dāmodara vrata, and that is the month dedicated to the sevā of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. So the month of Kārtika goes from Pūrṇimā to Pūrṇimā. So if we will begin the our Cāturmāsya on the Ekādaśī, then we'll have to complete the Cāturmāsya on the Ekādaśī but there is still four more days left in the month of Kārtika. Or even though the option (..) has been given to begin on this day, but out of the great honor and desiring, intensely desiring to attain Rādhā dāsyam, the service of Śrīmatī Rādhikā, we will begin our Cāturmāsya vrata from the Guru Pūrṇimā and finish on the Kārtika Pūrṇimā.
caturmasya-vows: Now, in this strict performance of Cāturmāsya, for the whole four months, one should not eat tomato, eggplant, the loki, parmal, (..), sesame, honey, etc. Honey. I said. Sesame. So, and but Śrīla A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda, when he came to the West, he thought to introduce everything is will be too much. So, he just gave certain restrictions within each month. So the first month is one should refrain from taking green leafy vegetables: spinach, cabbage, and so on. And, then, yogurt, milk, and urad dāl. In the other months. Śrīla Gurudeva, this was Śrīla Prabhupāda's standard. But my Gurudeva, he insisted all the devotees, especially the devotees who are staying in India, they should follow Cāturmāsya very strictly. And if they're in the West, then they can try as best they can.
brahmacari-sannyasi-vows: Now, you have to understand this. The reason we follow Cāturmāsya, it's not that these particular things, as we mentioned before in regard to the sesame seeds, it's not some special biological formula that at that time it will help with your bhakti. But the thing is this, that Caitanya Mahāprabhu did it. Our Parama Gurudeva did it, our Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura did it. And so because they did it, when we follow them, we accept their ānugatya, it increases our mamatā for them. It increases our possessiveness for them. This is what my Gurudeva did. This is what my paramparā does. This is what my Caitanya Mahāprabhu has done. Just like in the middle of Cāturmāsya, in (..) the full moon (..) in the middle, it's the Viśvarūpa Mahotsava. So it's not the day that Viśvarūpa took sannyāsa. It's not even the day that he passed away. But it's the day that Caitanya Mahāprabhu when He was on tour and He was in Paṇḍharpura, He heard the news that (..) His brother Viśvarūpa had passed away in Paṇḍharpura. He actually entered into the date of Viṭṭhala there. But (..) the because Mahāprabhu heard that His brother had passed away at that time, then He shaved His head. Right? Because if a family member passes away, then you shave your head. So we also, even though you're not supposed to shave for the whole Cāturmāsya, but we shave our heads on the full moon in the middle of Cāturmāsya. Why? Because Mahāprabhu did. To have that mamatā that we're in the family of Mahāprabhu. And His elder brother is so dear to Him passed away. So it's not the regulation itself that has the potency, but it's obeying the regulation that (..) nourishes our possessiveness, our mamatā for Caitanya Mahāprabhu.
kartika-niyama-seva:
By the causeless mercy of Śrī Guru and Gaurāṅga, during this month of Kārtika, every day we come before Śrī Kṛṣṇa with a dīpa in our hand and we offer the dīpas to His lotus feet, and we sing the Śrī Dāmodarāṣṭakam. Because this injunction has been given in Hari-bhakti-vilāsa, and there, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmīpāda said this is an essential part of the Dāmodara-vrata.

This month of Kārtika is also known as Dāmodara-māsa, the month of Dāmodara. Because dāma means rope and udara means belly. Dāmodara is the name of Kṛṣṇa who was bound around the belly by a rope, by His mother, Yaśodā. Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is unlimited and infinite, yet He is bound, not by rope, but by prema. So, those who, in this Dāmodara-māsa, month of Dāmodara, will sing the Dāmodarāṣṭakam with a pure heart, then they can please Lord Dāmodara and they can please Śrīmatī Rādhikā, and by the mercy of Śrīmatī Rādhikā, then Kṛṣṇa can be bound with the ropes of love in the heart of that devotee. So, this Dāmodara-vrata is extremely powerful, such that the all-powerful Supreme Lord becomes helpless in the presence of the devotee who follows this vrata.
purusottama-masa:
So then Śrī Kṛṣṇa said to Lord Nārāyaṇa, "Oh Ramāpati, just as I am celebrated in the world by the name Puruṣottama, so simply this month, this adhika-māsa will now also be renowned by the name Puruṣottama, the supreme person. And I am offering all my qualities to this month. And from today on, just as I am the source of all incarnations and whatever qualities the other incarnations have, they come from me, so I am superior. So in the same way, this month will be superior to all other months. All the other months, they are sakāma, they grant worldly desires. But this month is niṣkāma. And so if someone will worship Krishna in the month of Puruṣottama niṣkāma without any desires, or if someone will worship Krishna during this month with desires, but because the month itself is niṣkāma, Krishna will arrange for all those desires to go away. And all one's karmas will be burned."

[…]

Krishna said, "Sometimes my devotees commit offenses. But in this month of Puruṣottama, the devotees will be protected from committing any offenses. So only greatly foolish persons will neglect in this month auspicious activities such as chanting japa.
vyasa-puja-meaning: By the causeless mercy of Śrī Guru and Gaurāṅga, we are celebrating today the Śrī Vyāsa-pūjā. See, the appearance day of Śrīla Vyāsadeva is observed, Vyāsa-pūjā is observed on the appearance day of Śrīla Vyāsadeva. But also, as practiced by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu himself, (..) He used to (..) perform the Vyāsa-pūjā on the individual birthday of his Guru Pāda Padma, Śrīla Īśvara Purīpāda. So, (..) we observe this tradition. Our Prabhupāda Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura has said that the Vyāsa-pūjā is not the day when Śrī Guru accepts the offerings and worship of his disciples, but rather Vyāsa-pūjā is the day when Śrī Guru engages all of his anugata-jana, all of those who are practicing bhakti under his guidance, he engages them in the worship of his guru and his entire guru-paramparā, all the way back to Brahmā, all the way back to Śrī Kṛṣṇa himself.
sapta-pancakam:
So we are indebted to many personalities. So in the seven groups of five, 7 times 5 means 35. So, (..) there is one group in the center, and then one group in the north, in the south, the east and the west, on the four sides of that central group. And then there are two groups either side on the south side. So we'll describe them one by one. The central group, the center of the central group is Kṛṣṇa. Then starting from the south and going around clockwise, there is a saṅkarṣaṇa, oh sorry, starting from (..) the east and going clockwise, there is Kṛṣṇa's catur-vyūha, Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha. Then to the south, the central personality is Śrīla Vyāsadeva. And starting from the east and going around, Paila Ṛṣi. That is the sage of the Ṛgveda. Then Vaiśampāyana. Then Jaimini. Vaiśampāyana is Yajurveda, then Jaimini means Sāmaveda, and finally Atharvaveda Sumantu Ṛṣi. Then, in the north, the central personality is Śukadeva Gosvāmī. Then starting from the east, Rāmānujācārya, Madhvācārya, Viṣṇu Svāmī and Nimbāditya. Then on the western side, the central personality is Sanat-kumāra. Sanaka-kumāra, yeah, and from going from east, Sanat-kumāra, Sanātana, Sanandana and Viṣvaksena. So then on the eastern side, one's own guru. And then around him, his parama-guru, parameṣṭhi-guru, parātpara-guru, and paramparā-guru. So, his guru and five and five, the next four members of paramparā. So the central one is called kṛṣṇa-pañcakam. Then with the four sampradāya-ācāryas and Śukadeva Gosvāmī is called ācārya-pañcakam. To the south, Vyāsadeva and his disciples, vyāsa-pañcakam. Then with the four Kumāras, sanakādi-pañcakam. And then on the right side, guru-pañcakam. In the east.

Now, in that was the method of worship on the Vyāsa-pūjā in ancient times. Each personality is represented by a kalaśa with a coconut. decorated with, (..) svastika in kuṅkuma and mango leaves, and with a flag with the names of all these personalities. So this ceremony will be doing (..) in the afternoon. And, (..) now, in the more recent times, to the five ancient pañcakam, there are two more. So the one on the eastern side, that is called tattva-pañcakam. So obviously the Pañca-tattva did not worship themselves. So our ācāryas have added the tattva-pañcakam. The central person is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, and then going around, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, śrīvāsādi-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda. And (..) on the western side, it is called upāsya-pañcakam. Upāsya means those personalities who are the object of our upāsanā, our worship. So, the central person is Śrī Guru. And then Gaura and Gadādhara, and Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Of course, Gaura-Gadādhara are Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. But for us in the following the line of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, our worshipful personalities are Guru and Gaura-Gadādhara, Rādhā and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.
vyasa-puja-order: This is a very ancient ceremony which is performed on (..) on the uh Vyāsa Pūjā Guru Pūrṇimā day. And uh even on this day, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Nityānanda Prabhu, they used to do this. There's a paddhati, a manual that they followed to do this. So our previous gurus acquired this manual, and so we follow the practice even Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda used to do on this day. But uh in this, 35 different personalities are honored and they're invited to be present into kalaśas with coconuts and mango leaves. But if you do everything with coconuts and kalaśas and mango leaves, then this ritual will fill the whole apartment. So, and that's what we In India, we do it like that in full scale. I think last year I was in Rome, right, so in Rome we did it also on the full scale. And you have seven (..) separate priests offering the worship uh to the to the 35 personalities, seven groups of five like this. But when Vṛndāvana Vilāsinī invited me to come here, I said, "That's impossible." "We can't There's no way we'll be able to do this ancient ritual in your small apartment, there'll be no room for the people, once all the coconuts are are set up." So, I said, "Can we just make a miniature version?" She said, "All right, I'll try." And there it is: the very first scaled down miniature version of the ancient Vedic Vyāsa Pūjā ceremony with the coconuts being substituted by walnuts. So, but it looks so beautiful. All the names of the rishis are on the flags. Perhaps these leaves are not mango leaves. Not so many mango trees growing in Switzerland. But anyway, it looks like the real thing just scaled down. When I look at it, I just kind of feel about 18 ft tall. So it's so beautiful. So at at the end of the seminar today, we'll we can all uh partake in this ceremony.
major-festivals: But you should know that in the eleventh canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, just before Kṛṣṇa is about to leave this world, then Uddhava says to Kṛṣṇa, "You explained so many philosophical points about meditation and yoga-sādhana and philosophy, but it's all very difficult. Please tell me the most effective and sure way to attain kṛṣṇa-prema." So then Kṛṣṇa He gave the supreme methodology. He said, "You should make Vaiṣṇava festivals." (..)? On the holy days such as Janmāṣṭamī, Rādhāṣṭamī and all these holy days, appearance and disappearance days of Vaiṣṇavas, come together with the Vaiṣṇavas. And you should have kīrtanas, you should have Harikathā, you should have mahāprasāda distribution. You should perform dramas, all of these things. And by this you will obtain kṛṣṇa-prema. The power of these festivals, it cannot be overestimated.
rupa-gosvami-festival: What is that mano-'bhīṣṭa of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu? Our Śrīla Gurudeva, nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ viṣṇupāda aṣṭottara-śata-śrī śrīmad rūpānuga-ācārya-varya Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, he very enthusiastically with so much taste traveled throughout the world to establish the bhakti as expressed by Rūpa Gosvāmī, rūpānuga-bhajana. You can see that when it was Rādhāṣṭamī, Śrīla Gurudeva used to organize very beautiful festival in India. When it was Janmāṣṭamī, also very beautiful festival for Kṛṣṇa's birthday. But when it came round to the disappearance day of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Gurudeva would organize a festival for five days, more emphasis. Even then Janmāṣṭamī or Rādhāṣṭamī or Gaura-pūrṇimā, any day, five days symposium he used to make and invite all the Vaiṣṇava scholars in our Gauḍīya line and from other sampradāyas, from Nimbārka-sampradāya, from Vallabha-sampradāya, to come and spend the time deliberating upon the revelations of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
guru-purnima-festival: By the causeless mercy of Śrī Guru and Gaurāṅga, today we are celebrating Śrī Guru-pūrṇimā. This is the day, traditionally, all disciples worship their guru on this day, because this day is the appearance day of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vedavyāsadeva, the compiler of the Vedas. So, the seat of the speaker of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is called the vyāsāsana, the seat of Śrīla Vyāsadeva. So, because all sad-guru, pure gurus, are the representatives of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, so they are worshipped on this day, His appearance day.
janmastami-nandotsava: Tonight, at midnight, Śrī Kṛṣṇa will appear. Don't think that Kṛṣṇa appeared more than 5,000 years ago. The pastimes of Kṛṣṇa are nitya, eternal realities. And when we engage, we become absorbed in hearing and chanting about them, then we can experience they're happening just now. So the Janmāṣṭamī-mahotsava, the festival of Janmāṣṭamī means the opportunity when Śrī Kṛṣṇa can make His appearance in all of our hearts. So for this, we are fasting, (..)? And singing kīrtana until midnight with a very strong desire, very strong hope that we can receive a sphūrti, or a momentary vision within our heart of the appearance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
jhulana-yatra: Today, we are celebrating Jhūlana-yātrā, the swing festival of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It has a very deep meaning. You see that in the summertime in Vṛndāvana, it's very hot. This heat is the heat of separation. And the grass, everything becomes dry. And people are thinking, "Oh, when will this heat be over?" And when the summer is coming to an end, then they look and they see gathering in the sky dark, black, fresh rain clouds. And seeing the fresh rain clouds, they are Ghanaśyāma. Then they know, now the heat of the summer will be over, they will get relief. So Rādhārāṇī's heat of separation will only go away when She sees Ghanaśyāma, Śrī Kṛṣṇa whose complexion is like a fresh rain cloud. Then the rain begins to fall. And when the rain falls, then suddenly, all the forest, everything becomes lush and green.
nauka-vilasa:
So, Śrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu has shown by His own pastimes how devotees in their sādhaka forms should make very beautiful festivals for the deities. And among them, this festival of the Naukā-vilāsa is so beautiful and one of the prominent festivals in that Mahāprabhu and His associates participated in.

So why are we saying this? Because this naukā-vilāsa is a līlā-vilāsa. Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are sitting together among with their sakhīs and riding in a boat and very pleasingly talking to each other, sometimes joking, sometimes frowning, sometimes quarreling, like this. Sometimes apparently competing with each other and sometimes coming in complete praṇaya with each other.
radhastami-festival: Today, we are celebrating the appearance of—that means, in terms of the līlā—the birthday of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. Śrī Rādhāṣṭamī Mahā-mahotsava kī jaya! Jaya! For this really to be the appearance of Rādhikā for us as individuals, then Rādhikā must appear within our hearts. That is the true celebration. Only those who have had the darśana of Rādhikā in their heart, they can say they have really celebrated the Rādhāṣṭamī festival.
